resources.string: A heads-up shortly before rain reaches you.
Rain and thunderstorms as they happen, updated every few minutes.
Follow where the rain is heading. In our experience, the first 45 minutes are pretty spot-on.
A heads-up before rain reaches you that disappears as soon as it stops.
Built and run by volunteers in their spare time.
To show your current location on the map, we need your permission.\n\nWe won\'t ever share or store your location data.

Get notified shortly before it starts raining where you are, even while meteocool is closed.\n\nFor that, your device will also ask for background location access. Don\'t worry, this won\'t drain your battery.
You can change this anytime in Settings.
Rain alerts check your location while meteocool is closed, about every 15 minutes. On the next screen, choose \"Allow all the time\".\n\nWithout it, alerts only follow you while the app is open.
The map could not load. Trying again…
To use the location button or auto-zoom, you need to allow access to Location in your device\'s Settings. We won\'t store or share any location information.
This Is Not a Real Storm
Demo Mode is on: the map replays a recorded storm as if it were happening now. Nothing it shows is current weather.
If you like, we can warn you about precipitation coming to your current location. For this, the app sends your location to our servers in the background.

Intensity Threshold:
Notify only about precipitation expected to be at least this intense.

Notification Timeframe:
How far ahead of the precipitation you want to be notified.

Rain alerts need notifications and location access. For alerts as you move while the app is closed, set location access to \"Allow all the time\" in Settings. You can still browse the map without these permissions.
Notification changes could not reach the server. Alerts may still use your previous settings. Check your connection and reopen the app to retry.

Changes the colormap of the precipitation on the map. Each bar runs from drizzle on the left to hail on the right.

Classic:
meteocool's own. Drizzle fades in, then blue, green, yellow and red, and white to purple for hail.

NWS Reflectivity:
The US National Weather Service's colors. Close to Classic, but drizzle is drawn solid instead of fading in.

PyArt StepSeq:
From the Py-ART radar toolkit. Brown, green, blue and purple bands, each from light to dark, so small changes in intensity stand out.

Homeyer (Color Vision Deficiency):
Green through yellow and orange to dark red, made to stay readable with color vision deficiency.

Lang:
Light blue through yellow to brown, also readable with color vision deficiency.
Describe your issue or suggestion here:\n
Current weather, with features still in development. Might cause unexpected behaviour. 🐛
A recorded storm, replayed as if it were happening now. Not current weather.
Takes effect right away: the map reloads, and rain alerts come from the selected mode.

Radar Poland · CC BY 4.0. The source of data is the Institute of Meteorology and Water Management – National Research Institute. Data from IMGW-PIB has been processed by meteocool.
Artwork designed by Freepik from Flaticon

Two-Finger Map Rotation:
Turn the map with two fingers. When off, north always stays up.

Auto-Zoom After Start:
Zoom to your location whenever the app opens or comes back to the foreground. Needs location access.
Uses Light or Dark to match your phone\'s appearance. Turn it off to pick a map yourself.

All maps are kept muted so the radar stays readable.

Light and Dark:
Land, water, motorways and borders, little else.

OpenStreetMap:
Like the classic OpenStreetMap, with land use, all roads, buildings and regional borders.

CyclOSM (Biking):
For outdoors: forests and parks in color, tracks and paths drawn, motorways pushed back.
Radar Switzerland, France, Czechia and Poland, delivered through it
Terrain in the 3D map · open elevation data, mostly CC BY 4.0. Tap for every source.
meteocool may only use your location while it is open, so rain alerts are for where you last opened it. For alerts wherever you are, set location access to \"Allow all the time\" in Settings.
